cat > .github/workflows/triage.yml <<'EOF'
---
name: triage

# pull_request_target runs in the context of the base repository, so the token
# can write to pull requests opened from forks. This is only safe because the
# workflow never checks out or executes code from the pull request, and
# untrusted values (title, username) are passed through env vars, never
# interpolated into the script.
on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened]

permissions: {}

jobs:
  triage:
    name: Welcome and label
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
      issues: write
    steps:
      - name: Comment and apply needs-triage label
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          PR_AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh label create needs-triage --color FBCA04 \
            --description "Awaiting maintainer triage" 2>/dev/null || true
          body="$(printf 'Welcome @%s, and thanks for your pull request!\n\nSummary: "%s"\n\nA maintainer will triage it soon.' \
            "$PR_AUTHOR" "$PR_TITLE")"
          gh pr comment "$PR_NUMBER" --body "$body"
          gh pr edit "$PR_NUMBER" --add-label needs-triage
EOF
cat >> README.md <<'EOF'

## Triage workflow

`.github/workflows/triage.yml` runs when a pull request is opened. It:

- posts a comment welcoming the author by username and repeating the pull request title as a summary;
- applies the `needs-triage` label (creating it if it does not exist).

It uses the `pull_request_target` trigger so the token has write access even
for pull requests opened from forks (the plain `pull_request` trigger gives
fork PRs a read-only token). For safety, the workflow never checks out or runs
code from the pull request, and passes the title and username through
environment variables rather than interpolating them into the script.
EOF
python3 -c "import yaml;yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/triage.yml'))" && echo ok

content.text:
I added `.github/workflows/triage.yml` and a "Triage workflow" section in the README. I only checked that the workflow file parses as YAML. I haven't run it, because that needs a real pull request on GitHub.

- **What it does on open:** it comments "Welcome @author…" followed by `Summary: "<PR title>"`, and it applies `needs-triage`. It creates the label first if the repo doesn't have it.
- **Forks:** the workflow uses the `pull_request_target` trigger. The plain `pull_request` trigger gives a fork's PR a read-only token, so the comment and label would fail.
- **Why that trigger is safe here:** the workflow never checks out or runs code from the PR. The title and username reach the script through environment variables, not inline `${{ }}` expansion, so a malicious PR title can't inject shell commands.
- **Permissions:** the workflow is limited to `pull-requests: write` and `issues: write`, and it only uses the preinstalled `gh` CLI.
